newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH STUDY SEES REGIONAL 1997 GROWTH 3.5-5.5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH STUDY SEES REGIONAL 1997 GROWTH 3.5-5.5 PCT.

text.p: The growth rate of economies in central Europe and Baltic states is likely to be between 3.5 and 5.5 percent this year against an average of four percent in 1996, the Polish government's analitical unit said in a report.

The Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) said the region would benefit from better economic climate in European Union countries over the next two years but that central European states are likely to grow faster than the Baltics.
"The growth will be fuelled by investment and improving work efficiency helped by the inflow of foreign capital," the report, released on Thursday said.
It said Croatia was likely to have the lowest inflation in the region at four percent with the Czech Republic, Macedonia, Slovakia and Slovenia at an expected 10 percent or lower.
The report also expects a further fall of inflaton in Poland, Hungary and the Baltic states, but noted high internal demand would make curbing price growth difficult.
The internal demand, although the main source of economic growth, was also responsible for the deterioration of the region's trade and current account balance, the report said.

The report also said the region's exports, consisting mainly of labour-intensive goods and raw materials would remain competitive only as long as labour costs in these countries stay well below EU levels.
